quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Diplomatic Performance Review] In Priya's performance review, her manager writes that she 'consistently meets expectations and shows enthusiasm for collaborative work,' while noting that she 'would benefit from taking greater initiative on independent projects going forward.' The review closes by encouraging her to 'continue building on this foundation' in the coming year.
quests.question: What tone does the manager's review most likely convey?
options: Unqualified, enthusiastic praise with no reservations.
A recommendation that Priya be let go.
Outright anger at Priya's performance.
Mild, constructive criticism wrapped in polite, encouraging language.
quests.correctAnswer: Mild, constructive criticism wrapped in polite, encouraging language.
quests.hint: Notice the specific phrase about needing to take 'greater initiative,' softened by encouraging language around it.
quests.explanation: Phrases like 'would benefit from' and 'continue building on this foundation' are common ways of delivering gentle criticism diplomatically, rather than harsh or purely positive feedback.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Note From the Pharmacist] The pharmacist attaches a handwritten note to Mrs. Alvi's prescription bag, reminding her that this particular medication 'works best when taken at the same time each day' and suggesting she 'pair it with an existing habit, like brushing her teeth.' Nothing on the printed label mentions either point.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the pharmacist's intentions?
options: She wanted to discourage Mrs. Alvi from taking the medication.
She believed the printed label was unnecessary.
She wanted to offer practical advice beyond what the standard label provides.
She was required by law to add this note.
quests.correctAnswer: She wanted to offer practical advice beyond what the standard label provides.
quests.hint: Think about why someone would add extra, personal advice on top of information already printed on the label.
quests.explanation: Adding a handwritten note with practical tips not found on the label suggests the pharmacist wanted to give Mrs. Alvi genuinely helpful advice beyond the standard information.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [An Advisory Nobody Is Discussing] The government's travel advisory for the coastal region is quietly updated from 'exercise normal precautions' to 'exercise increased caution,' a change that receives no mention in mainstream news coverage, though several travel forums begin discussing it within hours of the update appearing online.
quests.question: What can be inferred about how this change is being noticed?
options: Travel forums removed all discussion of the update.
It received extensive mainstream news coverage immediately.
It is drawing more attention from everyday travelers than from major news outlets.
It has been completely ignored by everyone.
quests.correctAnswer: It is drawing more attention from everyday travelers than from major news outlets.
quests.hint: Compare the lack of mainstream coverage with the quick discussion appearing on travel forums.
quests.explanation: Forums discussing the change within hours, despite no mainstream news coverage, suggests everyday travelers are picking up on it more quickly than major outlets.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Three-Star Review] The online review reads: 'The blender works fine, I suppose, if you don't mind replacing the blades every few months and don't mind the odd burning smell after ten minutes of use. Customer service was polite when I called, for what that's worth.' The reviewer awards it three out of five stars.
quests.question: What is the overall tone of this review?
options: Genuinely enthusiastic and highly satisfied.
Sarcastic and unenthusiastic, despite the moderate star rating.
Completely neutral with no clear opinion.
Focused entirely on praising the product's durability.
quests.correctAnswer: Sarcastic and unenthusiastic, despite the moderate star rating.
quests.hint: Notice phrases like 'I suppose' and 'for what that's worth,' and think about what tone they usually signal.
quests.explanation: Phrases like 'I suppose' and 'for what that's worth,' paired with complaints about blades and burning smells, signal a sarcastic, unimpressed tone despite the moderate rating.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Quiet Change in Bedtime Stories] For years, Grandpa told wildly exaggerated stories about his youth at bedtime, each retelling more dramatic than the last. Lately, his grandchildren notice he sticks to shorter, simpler versions and sometimes forgets how a story ends partway through, quietly asking them to remind him.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the change in Grandpa's storytelling?
options: It may reflect changes in his memory rather than a change in his personality.
He has decided the exaggerated versions were inappropriate.
The grandchildren have stopped wanting to hear stories.
He has simply lost interest in telling stories.
quests.correctAnswer: It may reflect changes in his memory rather than a change in his personality.
quests.hint: Think about what forgetting details and needing reminders, rather than choosing shorter stories on purpose, suggests.
quests.explanation: Needing reminders and forgetting how stories end suggest the shift may be linked to changes in memory rather than simply a stylistic choice.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [An Update That Asks for More] The app's newest update introduces a feature explaining that it now needs access to contacts 'to improve your experience,' though the feature it unlocks, sharing scores with friends, has existed for two years using a much narrower permission that users could decline more easily.
quests.question: What can be inferred about this update's request for contact access?
options: It is essential and was never possible without this access before.
It reduces the amount of data the app collects.
It may be requesting more access than the stated feature actually requires.
It has no connection to any existing feature.
quests.correctAnswer: It may be requesting more access than the stated feature actually requires.
quests.hint: Think about what it means that the same feature worked for two years with a narrower permission.
quests.explanation: The same score-sharing feature working for two years with a narrower permission suggests this new, broader request for contacts may not be strictly necessary for that feature.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Memo About Flexibility] The company memo announces a new 'core hours' policy, requiring all employees to be online between 10 a.m. and 3 p.m., while emphasizing in bold that the company 'deeply values flexibility and trusts employees to manage their own schedules.'
quests.question: What can be inferred about the actual effect of this policy?
options: It matches exactly what the bolded language describes.
It removes all scheduling requirements entirely.
It introduces more scheduling structure than the language about flexibility suggests.
It gives employees complete control over every hour of their day.
quests.correctAnswer: It introduces more scheduling structure than the language about flexibility suggests.
quests.hint: Compare the specific requirement of fixed hours with the general language about valuing flexibility.
quests.explanation: Requiring set hours while emphasizing 'flexibility' in bold suggests the policy introduces more structure than the surrounding language implies.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Doctor's Careful Wording] After reviewing the scan, the doctor tells Mr. Farah that the results are 'not immediately concerning' but that she would 'feel more comfortable' scheduling a follow-up scan in three months rather than the standard yearly interval, adding that this is simply her 'usual practice for thoroughness.'
quests.question: What can be inferred about the doctor's level of concern?
options: She believes the results are seriously alarming.
She likely has some mild concern, even though she avoids stating it directly.
She has absolutely no concern about the results.
She is following a schedule identical to every other patient's.
quests.correctAnswer: She likely has some mild concern, even though she avoids stating it directly.
quests.hint: Think about what shortening the usual follow-up interval, despite calling the results 'not immediately concerning,' suggests about her actual level of caution.
quests.explanation: Shortening the follow-up interval well below the standard, despite describing the results calmly, suggests the doctor holds some mild concern she is choosing not to state outright.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Trailer That Undersells Itself] The studio's marketing team releases a trailer for the low-budget comedy without a single joke, relying instead on quiet, contemplative music and slow-motion shots, a marketing approach usually reserved for serious dramas rather than comedies.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the studio's confidence in marketing this comedy?
options: They believe the film has no dramatic elements at all.
They may not be confident that showcasing its comedic elements would attract an audience.
They used the exact same approach as their previous comedies.
They are extremely confident in the film's comedic strength.
quests.correctAnswer: They may not be confident that showcasing its comedic elements would attract an audience.
quests.hint: Think about why a comedy's trailer would borrow techniques normally used for serious dramas instead.
quests.explanation: Using a dramatic marketing style, rather than highlighting jokes, for a comedy suggests the studio may lack confidence that the humor alone would draw an audience.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Notice at the Trailhead] A newly posted sign at the trailhead reads: 'Wildlife activity has increased in this area. Hikers are strongly encouraged, though not required, to carry deterrent spray and avoid hiking alone before dusk.' The sign is dated only two days after a nearby ranger station reported an unusual sighting.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the timing of this sign?
options: It has been posted at this trailhead for many years.
It is completely unrelated to any recent events.
It is likely a direct response to the recent sighting.
It requires hikers to carry deterrent spray by law.
quests.correctAnswer: It is likely a direct response to the recent sighting.
quests.hint: Think about what posting the sign just two days after the sighting suggests about why it appeared now.
quests.explanation: A new sign appearing just two days after an unusual wildlife sighting was reported suggests the two events are likely connected.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Rubric With No Surprises] Ms. Whitfield hands back the essays with a rubric attached to each one, showing exactly which criteria earned full marks and which fell short, a level of detail her students say is far more specific than the brief handwritten comments she gave at the start of the semester.
quests.question: What can be inferred about Ms. Whitfield's grading approach this semester?
options: It has become more detailed and transparent over time.
It has remained exactly the same all semester.
It has become less detailed than before.
She has stopped grading essays altogether.
quests.correctAnswer: It has become more detailed and transparent over time.
quests.hint: Compare the detailed rubric now with the brief handwritten comments described from earlier in the semester.
quests.explanation: A detailed rubric replacing brief handwritten comments suggests Ms. Whitfield's grading approach has become more thorough and transparent as the semester progressed.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Town Hall That Ran Long] The town hall meeting, originally scheduled for ninety minutes to discuss a proposed parking fee, runs nearly three hours after residents line up at the microphone one after another, and the council ultimately agrees to revisit the proposal at a later date rather than voting that night.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the council's decision to delay the vote?
options: The council had already planned to delay the vote before the meeting began.
The meeting ended early with no discussion at all.
The strong turnout and lengthy discussion likely influenced them to reconsider.
No residents attended the meeting to share their opinions.
quests.correctAnswer: The strong turnout and lengthy discussion likely influenced them to reconsider.
quests.hint: Think about what a meeting running twice as long as planned, due to resident input, suggests about why the vote was postponed.
quests.explanation: A meeting stretching to three hours because of resident turnout, followed by a delayed vote, suggests the council's decision was likely influenced by that response.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Menu Description That Says Little] The new item on the menu is described only as 'chef's seasonal creation, market price,' offering no further detail about ingredients or preparation, a stark departure from the restaurant's usual practice of listing every component in detail.
quests.question: What can be inferred about this particular dish?
options: It has remained completely unchanged since the menu was created.
It likely changes frequently or uses ingredients that vary too often to describe precisely.
It uses the exact same ingredients as every other dish on the menu.
It has a lower price than every other item on the menu.
quests.correctAnswer: It likely changes frequently or uses ingredients that vary too often to describe precisely.
quests.hint: Think about why a restaurant that normally lists every detail would suddenly describe one dish so vaguely.
quests.explanation: A vague description and variable 'market price,' unlike the restaurant's usual detailed listings, suggest this dish likely changes often depending on available ingredients.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Reassuring Follow-Up Call] Two days after Mr. Odom's surgery, the clinic calls to check on his recovery, something he later learns is not standard practice for his type of procedure, according to a nurse friend who works at a different hospital.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the clinic's follow-up call?
options: It was required by law for this type of procedure.
It indicates something went wrong during his surgery.
It reflects a level of care beyond what is typically required.
It is a routine call given to every patient regardless of procedure.
quests.correctAnswer: It reflects a level of care beyond what is typically required.
quests.hint: Think about what learning this call is 'not standard practice' suggests about the clinic's approach.
quests.explanation: Learning that this type of follow-up call isn't standard for his procedure suggests the clinic went beyond typical requirements to check on his recovery.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Setting That Nobody Reads About] Deep within the smart speaker's settings, a toggle labeled 'Improve voice recognition by sharing anonymized recordings' is switched on by default, a detail mentioned nowhere in the product's marketing materials or the quick-start guide included in the box.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the company's approach to this setting?
options: It highlights this setting prominently in its marketing.
It wants every customer to know about this setting immediately.
This setting is turned off by default for all users.
It may prefer that most users remain unaware the setting exists.
quests.correctAnswer: It may prefer that most users remain unaware the setting exists.
quests.hint: Think about what omitting this detail from marketing materials and the quick-start guide suggests about how visible the company wants it to be.
quests.explanation: Leaving a default-on data-sharing setting out of both marketing materials and the quick-start guide suggests the company may prefer it goes unnoticed by most users.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Toast That Avoids the Obvious] At the retirement party, colleague after colleague gives a toast praising Mr. Callahan's 'dedication' and 'reliability' over thirty-two years, yet not a single speech mentions his sense of humor or personality, topics that dominate every other retirement party the office has held.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the tone of Mr. Callahan's retirement party?
options: It confirms he was known primarily for his humor.
It shows that no one at the office knew Mr. Callahan well.
It may reflect a more reserved or less personal reputation than other retirees had.
It reflects the exact same tone as every other retirement party.
quests.correctAnswer: It may reflect a more reserved or less personal reputation than other retirees had.
quests.hint: Compare what these speeches focus on with what typically gets mentioned at other retirement parties in this office.
quests.explanation: Focusing only on dedication and reliability, while skipping the personal, humorous notes common at other parties, suggests Mr. Callahan may have been remembered in a more reserved, professional light.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Deadline Extended Without a Request] Without anyone on the team asking, the project manager quietly moves the internal deadline back by a week after noticing two team members mention feeling stretched thin during a casual conversation in the break room.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the project manager's decision?
options: She was unaware of how the team was feeling.
She moved the deadline earlier, not later.
She was formally asked by the team to extend the deadline.
She acted on an overheard concern rather than a formal request.
quests.correctAnswer: She acted on an overheard concern rather than a formal request.
quests.hint: Think about what prompted her decision, given that no one directly asked for the extension.
quests.explanation: Extending the deadline right after overhearing team members mention feeling stretched thin, without a formal request, suggests she acted proactively based on that overheard concern.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Franchise That Won't Let Go] Despite three consecutive films earning lower box office returns than their predecessors, the studio announces a fourth installment, along with a spin-off series and a themed attraction at its amusement park, investments that suggest confidence the declining numbers don't fully reflect.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the studio's reasoning for continuing the franchise?
options: They have decided to end the franchise after the third film.
Box office returns have improved with each film.
They believe the declining numbers accurately predict future failure.
They likely believe the franchise's value extends beyond box office numbers alone.
quests.correctAnswer: They likely believe the franchise's value extends beyond box office numbers alone.
quests.hint: Think about what continuing to invest heavily, despite declining numbers, suggests about what the studio values in this franchise.
quests.explanation: Investing in a spin-off and a themed attraction despite declining box office returns suggests the studio sees value in the franchise beyond ticket sales alone.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Prescription Changed Quietly] Mrs. Delacroix's pharmacy switches her medication to a generic version without informing her directly, something she only discovers when the pill looks different, though a small note on the receipt, easy to overlook, does mention the substitution.
quests.question: What can be inferred about how clearly this change was communicated?
options: She was called personally to approve the change.
It was never disclosed anywhere at all.
It was clearly and directly explained to her beforehand.
It was disclosed, but not in a way likely to catch a patient's attention.
quests.correctAnswer: It was disclosed, but not in a way likely to catch a patient's attention.
quests.hint: Think about the difference between technically disclosing something and communicating it in a way someone would actually notice.
quests.explanation: A note on the receipt that is 'easy to overlook' means the substitution was technically disclosed, but not communicated clearly enough for most patients to notice right away.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Refund That Comes with Strings] The airline's email confirms a refund for the cancelled flight but specifies it will arrive as travel credit rather than cash, valid only for flights booked within the next twelve months, a detail placed in the final paragraph after two paragraphs of apology.
quests.question: What can be inferred about how the airline structured this email?
options: The email offered a full cash refund with no restrictions.
The less favorable details were placed where they are less likely to be noticed first.
The most important restriction was placed at the very beginning.
The apology paragraphs contained the refund's key restrictions.
quests.correctAnswer: The less favorable details were placed where they are less likely to be noticed first.
quests.hint: Think about where the restriction is placed within the email and why that positioning might matter.
quests.explanation: Placing the credit-only restriction after two paragraphs of apology suggests the airline structured the email so the less favorable detail is easier to miss.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Return Policy in Fine Print] The website's homepage advertises 'hassle-free returns' in large, bold letters, but the actual return policy, found only by scrolling to the bottom of the page and clicking a small link, requires items to be returned within seven days and excludes several popular categories entirely.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the gap between the advertised message and the actual policy?
options: The return policy applies equally to every category with no exceptions.
The full policy is more restrictive than the prominent advertising suggests.
The advertised message understates how generous the policy actually is.
The full policy matches the advertised message exactly.
quests.correctAnswer: The full policy is more restrictive than the prominent advertising suggests.
quests.hint: Compare the bold, simple advertising claim with the specific restrictions buried in the actual policy.
quests.explanation: A bold 'hassle-free' claim contrasted with a restrictive, hard-to-find policy suggests the advertising presents a more generous picture than the actual terms support.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Performance Bonus, Sort Of] The company announces 'record profits' in its quarterly email to staff, then follows with a note that annual bonuses this year will be 'adjusted to reflect evolving business priorities,' without specifying whether that means an increase or a decrease from previous years.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the likely direction of this year's bonuses?
options: Bonuses were eliminated entirely with no further mention.
The wording clearly confirms a significant increase in bonuses.
The company explicitly promises bonuses will stay the same.
The vague wording may be intended to soften news of a reduction.
quests.correctAnswer: The vague wording may be intended to soften news of a reduction.
quests.hint: Think about why a company reporting record profits would use vague language instead of directly stating good news about bonuses.
quests.explanation: Vague phrases like 'adjusted to reflect evolving priorities,' especially right after announcing record profits without linking the two, often soften unwelcome news, suggesting bonuses may be decreasing rather than rising.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Photo Album Left Open] After the argument, Dad leaves the old photo album open on the kitchen table to a page showing the whole family at the beach the summer before everyone got busy with separate lives, then quietly goes to bed without saying anything more about it.
quests.question: What can be inferred about Dad's intention in leaving the album open?
options: He was cleaning the kitchen and forgot the album was there.
He wanted to start a new argument about the photos.
He wanted to remind the family of a closer time without directly confronting anyone.
He wanted to hide the album from the rest of the family.
quests.correctAnswer: He wanted to remind the family of a closer time without directly confronting anyone.
quests.hint: Think about what leaving a meaningful photo open, right after an argument, without saying anything, suggests about his goal.
quests.explanation: Leaving the album open to a meaningful photo, right after an argument and without further comment, suggests Dad wanted to gently remind the family of closeness, rather than confront them directly.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Setting Hidden Behind a Toggle] The fitness app's default settings automatically share workout locations with all followers, a detail users only discover after a security researcher points out that the relevant privacy toggle is nested three menus deep and labeled with technical jargon rather than plain language.
quests.question: What can be inferred about how easily users could protect their location privacy?
options: It was more difficult than it should have been to find and adjust.
Location sharing was turned off by default for all users.
The app provided no way to adjust this setting at all.
It was clearly labeled and easy for every user to find.
quests.correctAnswer: It was more difficult than it should have been to find and adjust.
quests.hint: Think about what being nested three menus deep and using technical language suggests about how accessible this setting really was.
quests.explanation: A setting buried three menus deep and labeled in technical jargon suggests it was more difficult than it should have been for typical users to locate and adjust.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Comment Left Unanswered] During the Q&A after her lecture, Professor Marsh answers every question fully except one about a recent controversy in her field, which she acknowledges briefly before saying only that 'there's a lot of nuance there' and moving to the next raised hand.
quests.question: What can be inferred about Professor Marsh's response to that particular question?
options: She did not hear the question being asked.
She likely chose to avoid giving a detailed answer on that topic.
She answered that question more thoroughly than any other.
She had never encountered this controversy before.
quests.correctAnswer: She likely chose to avoid giving a detailed answer on that topic.
quests.hint: Compare how she handled this question with how fully she answered every other question.
quests.explanation: Giving a brief, vague answer and quickly moving on, unlike her thorough responses to other questions, suggests she deliberately chose not to elaborate on that particular topic.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Ticket Price That Keeps Climbing] The concert's ticket price on the resale site rises every time Farrukh refreshes the page, climbing nearly 20 percent in the ten minutes he spends deciding whether to buy, with a small banner now reading 'Only 3 tickets left at this price!'
quests.question: What can be inferred about this pricing pattern?
options: It guarantees the price will continue falling if he waits.
It shows the tickets are becoming less popular over time.
It reflects a completely random, unrelated coincidence.
It may be designed to create a sense of urgency to purchase quickly.
quests.correctAnswer: It may be designed to create a sense of urgency to purchase quickly.
quests.hint: Think about what a rising price combined with a 'limited tickets' banner is designed to make a buyer feel.
quests.explanation: A steadily rising price paired with a 'limited tickets' banner suggests the site may be designed to pressure buyers into purchasing quickly out of urgency.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Volunteer List That Grows Quietly] The community center's volunteer coordinator never advertises the need for more tutors, yet the list of volunteers doubles after a single tutor posts about her experience on a local parents' group, describing it only as 'the best hour of my week.'
quests.question: What can be inferred about the effect of the tutor's post?
options: The coordinator specifically asked her to write the post.
Her genuine, personal endorsement likely motivated others to sign up.
The post was ignored by everyone who saw it.
The volunteer list had already been growing before her post.
quests.correctAnswer: Her genuine, personal endorsement likely motivated others to sign up.
quests.hint: Think about what a heartfelt, personal comment, shared without any official request, achieved for recruitment.
quests.explanation: The volunteer list doubling right after a genuine, personal endorsement, without any official advertising, suggests her post likely motivated others to join.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Chart That Tells Two Stories] The clinic's patient satisfaction chart shows scores climbing steadily for the last three years, a trend proudly displayed in the waiting room, though a smaller chart in the same report, rarely mentioned aloud, shows average appointment length shrinking by nearly a third over that same period.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the relationship between the two charts?
options: The two charts are entirely unrelated measurements.
Shorter appointments always lead to lower satisfaction.
Higher satisfaction scores may not necessarily reflect longer, more thorough visits.
Both charts show identical, matching trends.
quests.correctAnswer: Higher satisfaction scores may not necessarily reflect longer, more thorough visits.
quests.hint: Think about why one chart is proudly displayed while the other is rarely mentioned, and what showing both together suggests.
quests.explanation: Satisfaction rising while appointment length shrinks, with only one chart prominently displayed, suggests the two trends may be connected in ways the clinic doesn't emphasize.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Contract Clause Nobody Mentions] During the sales pitch, the representative emphasizes the software's 'flexible monthly plan' repeatedly, but the contract Mr. Whitaker later reviews includes an automatic annual renewal clause requiring sixty days' written notice to cancel, a detail never raised verbally.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the sales pitch compared to the actual contract terms?
options: The pitch emphasized flexibility more than the contract's terms actually support.
The sales representative read the entire contract aloud.
The contract offers more flexibility than the pitch described.
The pitch and the contract terms matched exactly.
quests.correctAnswer: The pitch emphasized flexibility more than the contract's terms actually support.
quests.hint: Compare the repeated emphasis on 'flexible' during the pitch with the renewal clause buried in the actual contract.
quests.explanation: Repeatedly emphasizing flexibility while omitting the automatic renewal clause suggests the verbal pitch presented a more flexible picture than the written contract actually supports.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [A Silence That Speaks] Every previous year, the airline's CEO records a lengthy year-end video thanking staff and outlining plans for the year ahead. This year, staff receive only a two-paragraph written statement, and several employees mention in an internal survey that the shift 'felt noticeably different.'
quests.question: What can be inferred about how staff perceived this year's communication?
options: They noticed and were affected by the reduced level of engagement.
They preferred the shorter written statement to the video.
They found this year's communication identical to previous years.
No employees noticed any difference in communication style.
quests.correctAnswer: They noticed and were affected by the reduced level of engagement.
quests.hint: Think about what employees explicitly commenting on the shift, in a survey, suggests about how noticeable and meaningful the change felt to them.
quests.explanation: Employees specifically describing the shift as 'noticeably different' in a survey suggests they picked up on and were affected by the reduced engagement from leadership this year.
